The offending vehicle involved in this case is a scooty bearing registration No. DL-12S-4462,
which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 Sh. Trilochan Singh Talwar, owned by Ms. Sonia Talwar and insured with respondent no.3 National Insurance Company Ltd.
Case of the claimant 3.
It is the case of the claimant that on 14.07.2020, he was going to his home from his office.

When he reached Nelson Mandela Road near JNU West Gate, Vasant Vihar Masoodpur Flyover, New Delhi, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-12S-4462, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from wrong side and hit him from front side due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that the claimant was taken to Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, New Delhi where his MLC was prepared by the doctors.

sentences.text: Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant.
The claimant examined himself as PW1.

He deposed that he was going to his home from his office and when he reached Nelson Mandela Road near JNU West Gate, Vasant Vihar Masoodpur Flyover, New Delhi, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-12S-4462, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from wrong side and hit him from front side due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
However, there was no effective cross-examination of the claimant with regard to negligence.
He denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to his own negligence.
15. In the case of Muddasani Venkata Narsaiah (D) Th. Lrs. vs. Muddasani Sarojana AIR 2016 SC 2250, decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court, the following was held :-

sentences.text: "16. Moreover, there was no effective cross- examination made on the plaintiff's witnesses with respect to factum of execution of sale deed, PW.1 and PW-2 have not been cross examined as to factum of execution of sale deed.
The cross- examination is a matter of substance not of procedure one is required to put one's own version in cross-examination of opponent.
The effect of non cross-examination is that the statement of witness has not been disputed.

The effect of not cross-examining the witnesses has been considered by this Court in Bhoju Mandal & Ors. v.
Debnath Bhagat & Ors. AIR 1963 SC 1906.

sentences.text: It has been further observed that even when the accused was acquitted in the criminal case, the same will have no effect on the assessment of liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.

20. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the petitioners and the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

ISSUE NO. 2 - Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
23.

As the issue No.1 has been decided in favour of the claimant, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
24. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

25.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 26.

Claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW1/1 has tendered on record his discharge summary Ex. PW1/B,
as per which the claimant was admitted in Indian Spinal Injuries Centre on 14.07.2020 and discharged on the same day where he was diagnosed with Ist Interphalangeal joint dislocation right foot.
27. Claimant has tendered on record his medical bills as Ex. PW1/F which are totaling to a sum of Rs.7,055/-.
The respondents have failed to lead any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, he is held entitled to Rs.7,055/- towards his medical expenses.
(ii) Loss of earnings 28.
The claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has deposed that he was working in MS Support Services Pvt. Ltd. and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
He has tendered on record copy of his employment ID card as Ex. PW1/I. During cross-examination
, he deposed that he has not filed his salary slip regarding his employment.
He has also tendered on record his educational qualification certificate, as per which he had passed 8th class.

29. Since the income of claimant has not been established on record, the Tribunal deems it appropriate to consider the minimum wages of non-matriculates in Delhi, which were Rs. 16,861/-
at the relevant time of accident.

sentences.text: Claimant in his affidavit deposed that he was unable to work properly due to the injuries sustained in the accident and now he is jobless.
During cross-examination, he admitted that he has not filed his leave record.
31. Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, this Tribunal deems it fit to compensate the claimant for loss of earnings equivalent to a period of three months.

Therefore,
under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs.50,583/- (Rs.16,861/- X 3).
(iii) Loss of future earnings 32.
As per disability certificate issued by Dr. RML Hospital, the claimant has no permanent physical disability from neurosurgery and orthopaedics side and has 1% disability from ENT side.
33. In order to prove the disability certificate, the claimant examined Dr. Ankur Gupta, Assistant Professor from Dr. RML Hospital as PW2 who has proved the disability certificate of claimant.
He deposed that the above disability may be due to general reason and not due to the accident as he had not suffered any ENT as per record.
He further deposed that there is no loss of working capacity due to the above disability.
He further deposed that the claimant can work in a normal manner and it does not impact on his working capacity.

34. In view of testimony of PW2, the Tribunal deems it appropriate to take the functional disability of claimant as 'NIL'.
35.
Accordingly, the claimant is held not entitled to any amount under this head.
(iv) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 36.
As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries in the accident.

Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/-
each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
Further, an amount of Rs.25,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.1,25,000/- under this head.
(v) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 37.

The claimant in his affidavit is silent with regard to the amounts spent towards conveyance,
special diet and attendant charges.
During cross-examination, he admitted that he has not filed bills towards conveyance, special diet and attendant charges.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the Vidhyanand Tiwari vs Trilocfhan Singh Talwar on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189482604/

ISSUE No. 3/Relief 39.

In view of foregoing discussion, the claimant is thus awarded a sum of Rs.2,57,638/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Seven Thousand Six Hundred Thirty Eight only) (Rs.7,055/- + Rs.50,583/- +
Rs.1,25,000/- + Rs.75,000/-) along with 7.5% interest from the date of filing of DAR.

However, it is directed that the amount of interim award and interest for the suspended period, if any, during the course of this inquiry, shall be liable to be excluded from the award amount.
RELEASE 40.
The entire awarded amount is directed to be released in the saving bank account of claimant through RTGS/NEFT or any other electronic mode.
LIABILITY 41.

During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company argued that the respondent no. 1 was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act has been invoked against respondent no. 1 by the Investigating Officer.
42. In this regard, respondent no. 3/Insurance Company examined Sh. Raghunath Pawar, Assistant Manager (Legal) from their company as R3W1.

He deposed that respondent no. 1 was driving under the influence of alcohol and IO has invoked Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act against the respondent no. 1 in the chargesheet and hence, they are not liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

43. A bare perusal of the charge-sheet shows that Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act was also invoked by the Investigating Officer against respondent no. 1, besides the other sections, as investigation reflected that respondent no. 1 was under influence of liquor at the time of accident.
44. Perusal of MLC reflects that the respondent no. 1 was drunk, but no test has been carried out for ascertaining the quantity of consumption of liquor by respondent no.1 at the time of accident.
The same has also not been proved by the Insurance Company.
Accordingly, it cannot be presumed that the respondent no. 1 was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident beyond permissible limit.
